question.text: Will SRS or DOE have publicly stated a cause for the October 28, 2026 Savannah River National Laboratory fire by November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any time from October 28, 2026 through November 13, 2026, Savannah River Site (SRS), the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Savannah River National Laboratory (SRNL), or an on-the-record representative of any of them publicly identified a cause of the October 28, 2026 fire at SRNL — that is, named the mechanism or condition that started the fire (for example an electrical fault, battery failure, equipment malfunction, chemical reaction, hot work, or arson) as its cause, probable cause, suspected cause, or preliminary finding. The statement may appear in an SRS news release listed at https://public.srs.gov/category/news-releases/ (or in the SRS notification banner at https://public.srs.gov/), on a DOE or SRNL website, or be attributed to one of those entities in reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Statements that the cause is still under investigation, unknown, or undetermined — and statements that only describe when, or in which room of the laboratory, the fire began — do not resolve Yes. If no qualifying statement has appeared by 11:59 p.m. US Eastern Time on November 13, 2026, the question resolves No.
question.fine_print: Statements by Savannah River Nuclear Solutions (SRNS, the SRS management contractor) or by SRNL's operating contractor count as statements by SRS. Unattributed leaks, reporting based solely on unnamed sources, and statements by advocacy groups (such as SRS Watch) or by individual SRS/DOE employees speaking in a personal capacity do not count.

## SRNL fire cause research (as of 2026-11-03)

As of today, no SRS, DOE, SRNL or SRNS source has said what caused the fire. Every on-the-record statement I found says only that an investigation is underway.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The SRS news-release page has two newer posts, both dated Nov 2: a new NNSA Field Office Manager and the 2027 public tours. Neither is about the fire. The only fire-related post is the Oct 28 "Emergency Response Event, News Releases #1, #2, and #3". The text visible to me gave no cause, and the releases give two different declaration times (5:07 p.m. and 5:39 p.m.). [SRS news releases](https://public.srs.gov/category/news-releases/)
- 2026-11-03: The SRS homepage has a "Notifications" heading with no text under it. The page does not mention a cause. [SRS homepage](https://public.srs.gov/)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Searches through Nov 3 found no statement of cause, probable cause or preliminary finding from SRS, DOE, SRNL or SRNS.
- 2026-10-29: Monte Volk, public affairs officer for DOE's Office of Environmental Management, said: "An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway." Under the criteria, this kind of statement does not count. No SRNS spokesperson was quoted. [Post and Courier/Aiken Standard](https://www.postandcourier.com/aikenstandard/aikenstandard/news/local/srnl-fire-srs-emergency-response/article_35bcf1f0-7957-470b-8d5c-5c89a441419c.html)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-31: The Current reported that "the size and cause of the fire are not yet confirmed" and that the materials involved are unknown. SRNL and DOE had not answered requests for comment beyond confirming the investigation. [The Current](https://thecurrentga.org/2026/10/31/as-safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-a-fire-erupts-at-savannah-river-site/) ([GPB version](https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/10/29/safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-fire-erupts-at-savannah))
- 2026-10-30: Autonocion reported that SRS and DOE had not said how the fire started or how it was put out. It mentioned that Building 773-A depends on the fire-water system, but did not say the fire happened there. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/75-year-old-nuclear-lab-fire-one-room-310-square-mile-site-emergency-four-hours-fire-water-pipes/)
- 2026-10-29/30: SRS Watch pointed to earlier DNFSB fire-suppression findings. SRNL has not confirmed any link to this fire. [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/watchdog-cites-earlier-fire-safety-001554587.html)
- 2026-10-29: WRDW's explainer says there is no public information tying any DNFSB-identified issue to the fire. It notes that investigations typically take weeks or months and that DNFSB may review the incident. [WRDW](https://www.wrdw.com/2026/10/29/what-we-know-about-emergency-savannah-river-site/)
- 2026-10-28: A DOE spokesperson said the fire was extinguished, no radiological contamination was reported, and one employee had minor injuries. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/savannah-river-nuclear-site-fire-no-contamination-detected-after-emergency-12633480), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/28/us/savannah-river-national-lab-fire-nuclear-south-carolina)

### 4. Base rates
- I could not find a systematic dataset on how quickly DOE sites name fire causes.
- 2006-01-10: After a flash fire with an injury at SRNL, the cause came out through a formal DOE Type B Accident Investigation report rather than an early press statement. I did not confirm when that report was published. [DOE](https://www.energy.gov/node/902681)
- In my background knowledge (not checked here), DOE did sometimes give early informal descriptions after the 2014 WIPP underground truck fire. The formal forensic and accident reports came weeks to months later. [WIPP forensic report](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2016/06/f33/WIPP-Fire-Forensic-Report-Final.pdf)
- So far SRS has said very little: three short releases, no room or material named, and no follow-up release in the six days since the fire. DNFSB resident-inspector weekly reports often describe causes, but DNFSB is not a qualifying source unless it attributes a finding to SRS or DOE.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question (New River Gorge, Port of Savannah, Rocket Lab and others) is related.

### 6. Upcoming events before Nov 13
- DNFSB weekly site reports for the weeks ending Oct 30 and Nov 6 are likely to be posted with a lag. If they cite the contractor's preliminary cause, outlets could report it as attributed to SRS or SRNS, but the report itself does not count.
- Follow-up from local outlets: WRDW has said it is pressing SRS about the reversal on the radiological release. The Aiken Standard is also covering the story.
- Possible further SRS news release or comment from SRNS or DOE.
- Congressional or state (SC Emergency Management Division) inquiries are possible. I found none scheduled.
- The Citizens Advisory Board meeting is on Nov 17, after the resolution deadline.

Sources: [SRS news releases](https://public.srs.gov/category/news-releases/), [SRS homepage](https://public.srs.gov/), [Post and Courier](https://www.postandcourier.com/aikenstandard/aikenstandard/news/local/srnl-fire-srs-emergency-response/article_35bcf1f0-7957-470b-8d5c-5c89a441419c.html), [The Current](https://thecurrentga.org/2026/10/31/as-safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-a-fire-erupts-at-savannah-river-site/), [GPB](https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/10/29/safety-oversight-wanes-and-nuclear-missions-accelerate-fire-erupts-at-savannah), [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/75-year-old-nuclear-lab-fire-one-room-310-square-mile-site-emergency-four-hours-fire-water-pipes/), [WRDW](https://www.wrdw.com/2026/10/29/what-we-know-about-emergency-savannah-river-site/), [WRDW Oct 28](https://www.wrdw.com/2026/10/28/emergency-response-activities-underway-srs/), [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/watchdog-cites-earlier-fire-safety-001554587.html), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/savannah-river-nuclear-site-fire-no-contamination-detected-after-emergency-12633480), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/28/us/savannah-river-national-lab-fire-nuclear-south-carolina), [DOE 2006 Type B](https://www.energy.gov/node/902681), [WIPP report](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2016/06/f33/WIPP-Fire-Forensic-Report-Final.pdf)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain (Nov 3 to 11:59 p.m. ET on Nov 13). For Yes, SRS, DOE, SRNL or SRNS (or an on-the-record spokesperson) must publicly name a mechanism as the cause, probable cause, suspected cause or preliminary finding. Examples would be an electrical fault, a chemical reaction or an equipment malfunction. It can appear in a release, on a website, or in credible reporting attributed to them.

(b) Status quo: No. Six days after the fire, the only on-the-record line is "an investigation into the cause of the fire is underway" (DOE EM's Monte Volk, Oct 29). There has been no follow-up news release.

(c) Base rate: DOE site fires and events tend to have causes disclosed through formal investigation reports weeks to months later. Early informal cause statements happen in only a minority of cases, often when the cause is mundane, such as an electrical or vehicle fire. For a cause to be named within about 2 weeks for a radiological-area event with contested messaging, I estimate roughly 20-25%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For No:**
  - SRS has been extremely reticent. Three short releases on Oct 28 named no room, building or material.
  - Nothing has come out since. The Nov 2 releases are on unrelated topics.
  - The Current (Oct 31) said the cause was "not yet confirmed."
  - WRDW (Oct 29) noted that investigations take weeks or months.
  - The release/no-release reversal gives the site an incentive to say little before a formal review.
  - The Nov 17 CAB meeting, the most natural venue for disclosure, falls after the deadline.
- **For Yes:**
  - The event was a Site Area Emergency and drew national coverage (CNN, Newsweek).
  - Local reporters are pressing actively, and a spokesperson could offer a preliminary description to reporters.
  - DNFSB weekly reports might relay contractor preliminary findings, which outlets could attribute to SRNS.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** SRS stays silent pending its internal investigation. The DNFSB weekly reports are posted with a lag or describe the event without the cause being attributed to SRS. Disclosure slips to the Nov 17 CAB meeting or a later report.
- **Yes:** Under pressure from WRDW or Aiken Standard follow-ups, an SRNS spokesperson says preliminary indications point to something like an electrical component or a chemical reaction in a hood. Alternatively, a news story quotes a DNFSB report stating "SRNS personnel determined…" and counts it as attributed.

(f) I start at about 22%. I move down because of the six days of silence, the absence of follow-up releases and the site's defensive posture after the radiological-release reversal. I add back a little for possible DNFSB-mediated attribution and for media pressure. Final: about 13%.

Probability: 13%
